manufacturer: Shenzhen Oculgen Biomedical Technology Co., Ltd.
mechanism: OCUL101 is an investigational intravitreal bi-specific humanized antibody-like trap designed to block VEGF-A and complement C5, targeting angiogenesis, vascular leakage, and complement-mediated inflammation in neovascular AMD with or without geographic atrophy.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists the STAT study (OCUL101-002; NCT07520318) as a 255-participant Phase 2/3 randomized, masked, active comparator-controlled study that is not yet recruiting, with estimated start April 17, 2026, primary completion February 1, 2029, and study completion March 29, 2029. Oculgen announced on May 5, 2026 that U.S. clinical sites were initiated and ready to enroll participants.
expected_launch_window: 2030-2032 if the STAT Phase 2/3 program is registrationally adequate and supports filing; no approval date disclosed
clinical_summary: OCUL101 is differentiated from standard anti-VEGF monotherapy by dual VEGF-A and C5 inhibition in a single intravitreal product, with the STAT study enrolling treatment-naive nAMD patients with or without quantifiable geographic atrophy and comparing OCUL101 dose strategies against aflibercept 2 mg. The trial's Part B primary efficacy endpoint is change from baseline in BCVA at Week 36 versus aflibercept, with secondary endpoints including CST, 15-letter BCVA gain, CNV lesion size, and square-root GA lesion-size change through Week 96. Oculgen reports completed Phase 1b SAD/MAD work with favorable safety, no DLTs, serious adverse events, or vision-threatening complications, durability beyond 17 weeks after one high dose, and repeated-dose BCVA/anatomic trends versus aflibercept, but no peer-reviewed or ClinicalTrials.gov results were found.
safety_summary: NCT07520318 has no posted results and Part A is explicitly designed around AE, SAE, and TEAE incidence through treatment and follow-up. Company-reported Phase 1b safety claims are favorable but preliminary. Intravitreal anti-VEGF analog labeling highlights endophthalmitis, retinal detachment/vasculitis, intraocular pressure increases, and arterial thromboembolic risk; complement-inhibitor analog labels and policies highlight endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, intraocular inflammation, increased intraocular pressure, and neovascular AMD. OCUL101-specific long-term ocular inflammation, C5-related, GA-progression, and bilateral-use safety remain open.
management_tools: Medical-benefit prior authorization for any future launch, with retina specialist prescribing or consultation
Require eye-specific diagnosis of neovascular AMD, baseline BCVA, OCT/CST, lesion imaging, and GA documentation when GA is part of the labeled population
Require exclusion of active ocular or periocular infection and active intraocular inflammation before dosing
Set dose, volume, treated-eye, and interval limits to the final label; avoid off-label monthly escalation or bilateral same-day assumptions unless supported
Require response-based continuation using BCVA maintenance or improvement, CST/anatomic response, CNV activity, GA lesion growth where applicable, and injection-frequency history
Preserve preferred lower-cost anti-VEGF pathways for patients without labeled need for dual VEGF/C5 inhibition
Track concomitant same-eye anti-VEGF or complement inhibitor use and prohibit duplicative therapy unless final labeling or evidence supports it
Prepare coding, buy-and-bill, site-of-care, and outcomes-tracking logic for intravitreal administration
evidence_gaps: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT07520318.
No peer-reviewed human OCUL101 efficacy or safety publication was found.
Oculgen's Phase 1b SAD/MAD claims are company-reported and not accompanied by detailed public patient counts, event tables, or full comparator methods.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists the study as not yet recruiting, while Oculgen announced that U.S. sites were initiated and ready to enroll.
It is unclear whether the 255-participant Phase 2/3 STAT study alone will be sufficient for U.S. registration or whether additional pivotal evidence will be required.
No disclosed U.S. price, net cost, contracting approach, labeled dosing interval, bilateral-eye policy, or duration limit exists for OCUL101.

sources.title: A Phase II/III Multicenter, Randomized, Masked, Active Comparator-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Two Doses of OCUL101 in Participants With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration With or Without Geographic Atrophy - STAT Study
supports: ClinicalTrials.gov ID is NCT07520318 and other study ID is OCUL101-002.
Lead sponsor and organization are Shenzhen Oculgen Biomedical Technology Co., Ltd.
Official title describes OCUL101 as an anti-VEGF and anti-complement C5 bi-specific humanized antibody-like trap for nAMD with or without GA.
Overall status is not yet recruiting; estimated start is 2026-04-17; estimated primary completion is 2029-02-01; estimated study completion is 2029-03-29.
Study type is interventional; phases are Phase 2 and Phase 3; design is randomized, parallel, quadruple-masked, active comparator-controlled.
Estimated enrollment is 255 adults aged 50 to 89 with treatment-naive CNV secondary to AMD, with or without GA.
Part A evaluates OCUL101 10.4 mg; Part B evaluates OCUL101 6.5 mg and 10.4 mg strategies against aflibercept 2 mg.
Primary outcomes are Part A AE/SAE/TEAE incidence and Part B BCVA change from baseline at Week 36 versus aflibercept.
Secondary outcomes include BCVA, CST, 15-letter BCVA improvement, CNV lesion size, and GA lesion-size change.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Oculgen Launches U.S. Phase II/III STAT Study to Advance Treatment for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration (nAMD)
supports: Oculgen announced the U.S. launch of the STAT Study on May 5, 2026.
The company stated clinical sites were activated and prepared to enroll participants.
STAT is described as a Phase II/III randomized, masked, active comparator-controlled trial of two OCUL101 dose levels.
OCUL101 is described as an investigational bi-specific antibody engineered to inhibit VEGF and complement C5.
The stated indication is neovascular AMD with or without geographic atrophy.
The company frames dual VEGF/C5 inhibition as a strategy to address angiogenesis and complement-mediated inflammation.

sources.title: Oculgen Announces Initiation of Phase II Clinical Trials for Novel Bispecific Antibody OCUL101 Worldwide
supports: Oculgen announced planned global Phase II initiation for OCUL101 in nAMD, DME, and GA.
OCUL101 is described as a novel bispecific antibody and a dual-mechanism antibody targeting three retinal conditions.
Oculgen stated it completed the Phase 1b MAD high-dose cohort of monthly intravitreal injections in China as part of an ongoing Phase 1b/2 nAMD trial.
The company reported favorable SAD and MAD safety with no dose-limiting toxicities, serious adverse events, or vision-threatening complications.
The company reported durability beyond 17 weeks after a single high dose and repeated-dose trends suggesting BCVA and anatomic superiority versus aflibercept.
The company stated CDE and U.S. FDA acceptance in February 2026 to initiate Phase II trials and planned April 2026 Phase II activity in China and the U.S.

sources.title: Oculgen Company Profile

The company profile states Oculgen is headquartered in Nanshan District, Shenzhen, with clinical operations in Shanghai and an R&D center in Zhuhai.
The company states its product portfolio covers ophthalmic drug discovery, preclinical models, scale-up production, formulation development, and commercialization.

sources.title: DailyMed: VABYSMO (faricimab-svoa) injection
supports: Vabysmo is a VEGF and Ang-2 inhibitor indicated for neovascular/wet AMD, DME, and macular edema following RVO.
Recommended nAMD dosing is 6 mg intravitreal injection every 4 weeks for the first 4 doses, followed by individualized dosing at Weeks 20/24/28/36/44 depending on disease activity.
Warnings include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, intraocular pressure increases, and arterial thromboembolic event risk.
Common adverse reactions include cataract and conjunctival hemorrhage.
Vabysmo is used as the closest marketed intravitreal bispecific anti-VEGF analog for OCUL101 cost and management assumptions.

sources.title: DailyMed: EYLEA (aflibercept) injection
supports: Eylea is a VEGF inhibitor indicated for neovascular/wet AMD.
Recommended nAMD dosing is 2 mg intravitreal injection monthly for the first 3 months, followed by every 8 weeks, with some patients needing monthly dosing after the first 12 weeks.
Warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachments, retinal vasculitis, intraocular pressure increases, and arterial thromboembolic event risk.
Common adverse reactions include conjunctival hemorrhage, eye pain, cataract, vitreous detachment, vitreous floaters, and increased intraocular pressure.
Eylea is the active comparator in NCT07520318 and represents standard anti-VEGF treatment burden.

sources.title: DailyMed: IZERVAY (avacincaptad pegol intravitreal solution)
supports: Izervay is a complement inhibitor indicated for geographic atrophy secondary to AMD.
The recommended dose is 2 mg by intravitreal injection to each affected eye once monthly.
Warnings include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, neovascular AMD, and increased intraocular pressure.
Common adverse reactions include conjunctival hemorrhage, increased IOP, blurred vision, neovascular AMD, punctate keratitis, and eye pain.
Izervay is used as a C5 complement-inhibitor analog for OCUL101 safety and management assumptions.

sources.title: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0701: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Inhibitors for Ocular Indications
supports: Aetna considers faricimab medically necessary for neovascular/wet AMD when criteria are met.

Aetna uses continuation criteria requiring positive clinical response such as improvement or maintenance in BCVA or visual field, reduced rate of vision decline, or reduced risk of more severe vision loss.
Aetna's Susvimo criteria require diagnosis of nAMD and prior response to at least two intravitreal VEGF inhibitor injections, illustrating payer controls for durable ocular VEGF approaches.
The policy supports medical-benefit prior authorization and response-based reauthorization for future OCUL101 management.

sources.title: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 1041: Avacincaptad Pegol (Izervay)
supports: Aetna requires precertification for Izervay in applicable plan designs.
Aetna requires Izervay to be prescribed by or in consultation with an ophthalmologist.
Aetna considers Izervay medically necessary for GA secondary to AMD and all other indications experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Aetna continuation requires positive clinical response, such as BCVA or visual-field maintenance/improvement, reduced rate of vision decline, or reduced risk of more severe vision loss.
Aetna states Izervay is more costly than Syfovre and requires contraindication, intolerance, or ineffective response to the lower-cost alternative in its commercial policy language.
The policy supports specialist, diagnosis, step-therapy, and response-based controls for OCUL101 if labeled for nAMD with GA.

expected_launch_window.value: 2030-2032 if the STAT Phase 2/3 program is registrationally adequate and supports filing; no approval date disclosed
expected_launch_window.method: Derived from Phase 2/3 status, estimated primary completion on 2029-02-01, estimated study completion on 2029-03-29, company-reported U.S. launch/site initiation in May 2026, and expected BLA/regulatory review timing after final efficacy and safety data.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A U.S. launch before 2030 is unlikely because the pivotal-looking study reads out in 2029 and no filing date or approval pathway has been disclosed.

annual_cost_range.method: Low estimate uses 6 first-year doses priced at the Vabysmo intravitreal bispecific anti-VEGF analog price of $2,357.65 per dose. High estimate uses 8 Vabysmo-priced anti-VEGF-like first-year doses plus 12 monthly Izervay C5 complement-inhibitor doses at $2,059.18, reflecting a conservative dual-pathway analog scenario for nAMD with GA.
annual_cost_range.explanation: OCUL101 has no disclosed price. The estimate is per treated eye, gross drug acquisition only, and excludes administration, imaging, bilateral treatment, rebates, discounts, wastage, complication management, and rescue therapy.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced OCUL101's single-product VEGF-A/C5 mechanism, inclusion of nAMD with or without GA, active aflibercept-controlled Phase 2/3 design, GA lesion-growth endpoints, and company-reported early safety/durability against absence of posted or peer-reviewed human results.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: If validated, dual VEGF/C5 inhibition could address exudation and complement-mediated atrophy risk in one intravitreal product, but current public clinical evidence is too immature for a High rating.

budget_impact.method: Assessed from likely branded intravitreal biologic pricing, prevalent nAMD population, possible nAMD-with-GA positioning, repeated first-year dosing, and potential substitution for or addition to high-cost anti-VEGF and complement pathways.
budget_impact.explanation: Even if restricted to specific nAMD or nAMD-with-GA segments, per-eye drug cost and broad ophthalmology utilization could create meaningful medical-benefit spend.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from Phase 2/3 status and potentially differentiated dual-pathway mechanism, offset by no posted results, no price, no approval date, and standard intravitreal administration logistics.
disruption_risk.explanation: OCUL101 could require new criteria for nAMD with GA and dual-pathway substitution, but near-term disruption is limited until Phase 2/3 efficacy and safety data mature.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action reflects active U.S. Phase 2/3 launch, expected 2029 readout, potentially high budget impact, and need to define dual VEGF/complement management logic before launch.
recommended_action.explanation: Begin preparatory monitoring and analog policy design, but defer final coverage criteria, step therapy, and contracting strategy until Phase 2/3 results, label, dosing interval, and price are available.

quality_flags: OCUL101 is investigational and not FDA-approved or marketed for nAMD as of 2026-05-28.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT07520318 as not yet recruiting, while Oculgen's May 2026 press release states U.S. sites were activated and ready to enroll.
The assigned asset name is generic on ClinicalTrials.gov, but the official title and company sources identify the asset as OCUL101.
Phase 1b efficacy and safety claims are company-reported; no detailed public dataset, peer-reviewed manuscript, or ClinicalTrials.gov results were found.

Annual cost estimate is analog-derived from marketed intravitreal anti-VEGF/bispecific and complement products and may materially differ from final OCUL101 price, dosing, net rebates, bilateral use, and administration costs.
Clinical differentiation depends on whether the Phase 2/3 STAT study confirms benefit versus aflibercept and demonstrates meaningful value for GA-related outcomes.
